routes.label: Subtract four quarter-disks from the square

question:
Four circles of radius \(3\) are arranged as shown. Their centers are the vertices of a square. The area of the shaded region is closest to

[Figure 1](figures/1992_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The square joining the centers gives a useful outer boundary for the shaded region. In the depicted arrangement, adjacent circles touch, so each side of the square consists of two radii. Its side length is therefore \(3+3=6\), and its area is \(6^2=36\).

At each corner, the square contains one quarter of a disk of radius \(3\), because a square's corner angle is \(90^\circ\). These four quarter-disks have no overlapping interiors, and together their area equals the area of one complete disk:
\[
4\left(\frac14\pi\cdot3^2\right)=9\pi.
\]
The shaded region is exactly what remains inside the square after these pieces are removed. Its area is
\[
36-9\pi\approx7.73.
\]
This is closest to \(7.7\), so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
